data.title: Resource shares help lift TSX to eight-day high
data.description:
By Sudeshna Ghoshal and Fergal Smith

Canada's main stock index rose to an eight-day high on Thursday, led by gains for energy and metal mining shares, as investors grew optimistic that market volatility would fade.

The S&P/TSX Composite Index ended up 246.89 points, or 0.7%, at 34,426.88, its highest closing level since November 18.

  • Stock markets in Europe and across Asia also rallied as the latest salvo of US tariffs looked less damaging than first feared and after the US Thanksgiving holiday appeared to offer a welcome break from AI jitters

  • "We're coming off quite a lot of volatility over the last week and you're seeing some big moves in commodity markets and the whole AI trade in the US has been quite volatile," said Michael Dehal, a senior portfolio manager at Dehal Investment Partners at Raymond James

  • "We do think that a lot of the excesses in the markets have been washed out and we could be set up for a year-end rally," Dehal said

  • The energy sector added 1.9% after Yemen's Houthis said they hit ​Saudi Arabia's largest oil refinery and Iran said mines struck ships in the Strait of Hormuz, boosting the price of oil. US crude futures were up 1.5% at $84.91 a barrel

  • The materials sector , which includes metal mining shares, gained 1.7% as copper prices rebounded on bargain hunting

  • Technology rose 0.9% and industrials (.GSPTTIN) ended 0.6% higher

  • Alimentation Couche-Tard does not plan to raise the price in its public tender offer for Polish convenience store operator Zabka or extend the acceptance period, CEO Alex Miller told Reuters. The company's shares rose 1.9%

data.title: President Trump Says Pre-Election GDP Numbers Were Fake, Seeks Probe On Commerce Department
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - U.S. President Donald Trump has accused the Commerce Department of releasing 'fake' economic growth figures just ahead of the midterm election on November 3 and sought an immediate investigation into the 'grave' matter.

In a post on the social media platform Truth Social, where he wished Thanksgiving, Trump said, 'Additionally, I would like to wish a Happy Thanksgiving to even those who issued fake Economic Numbers, just prior to the Election, and corrected them yesterday, three weeks late.'

Revised data from the Commerce Department showed on Wednesday that the third quarter gross domestic product growth figure was revised to 4.3 percent from the initially estimated 3.4 percent.

Trump called this 'A record setting error, and one so grave that it should be immediately investigated.'

In a post on the same platform earlier on Thursday, Trump said, 'The American Economy under The Trump Administration is doing far better than the good numbers already released.'

The president questioned why the correct number was not released before the election and sought an immediate investigation. 'This is not a small error, this is a massive, and purposeful, error,' he added.

The Commerce Department routinely revises GDP figures as new and detailed data from various sectors become available and the agency follows its own schedule to release the revised data.

Trump has repeatedly tried to cast doubts on economic indicators that does not favor his administration and is now seeking to put the blame for Republicans' poor performance in the midterm elections on the GDP estimates.

data.title: First Helium Provides Update on Pending Acquisition and Trading Halt
data.description:
CALGARY, AB / ACCESS Newswire / November 26, 2026 / First Helium Inc. ("First Helium" or the "Company") (FRA:2MC) provides an update further to its news release dated October 14, 2026, announcing that the Company, through its wholly-owned subsidiary First Helium Alberta Inc., entered into a definitive purchase and sale agreement to acquire shallow heavy oil assets in the Company's core Worsley area of northern Alberta (the "Acquisition").

As previously disclosed, the Company has engaged Sproule ERCE, an independent qualified reserves evaluator, to prepare an evaluation of the assets to be acquired in accordance with National Instrument 51-101 - Standards of Disclosure for Oil and Gas Activities for filing with the TSX Venture Exchange (the "TSXV"). The evaluation is not yet complete. Upon its completion, the Company intends to file the evaluation and related materials with the TSXV.

Trading in the Company's common shares remains halted pending completion of the evaluation report. Trading will remain halted until the TSXV is satisfied that the Company has met its filing requirements. The Company will provide a further update when the evaluation is complete or as otherwise required.

Completion of the Acquisition remains subject to a number of conditions, including TSXV acceptance, completion of financing, and Alberta Energy Regulator licence transfer approvals and related security requirements, as described in the Company's October 14, 2026 news release.

ABOUT FIRST HELIUM

Led by a senior executive team with extensive experience in oil and gas exploration and operations, mining, finance and capital markets, First Helium is pursuing a shallow heavy oil growth strategy while preserving the option to develop its premium North American helium-enriched natural gas assets.

First Helium holds more than 30,000 acres along the highly prospective Worsley Trend in northern Alberta, which has been the focus of the Company's exploration and development drilling activities.

Building on its 7-30 shallow heavy oil discovery, 15-25 helium discovery, 1-30 and 4-29 light oil wells, and 5-27 helium-enriched natural gas evaluation well, the Company has identified follow-up drilling locations and acquired infrastructure to support future development at Worsley. Cash flow from the Company's Worsley oil wells has helped advance its ongoing exploration and development strategy.

data.title: TC Energy announces second Indigenous investment in Coastal GasLink
data.description:
Agreement with 12 British Columbia First Nations marks another milestone in Indigenous participation in Canadian energy infrastructure

CALGARY, Alberta, Nov. 26, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- TC Energy Corporation (TSX, NYSE: TRP) (TC Energy or the Company) today announced the closing of an agreement with CGL First Nations Limited Partnership (CGL FNLP), an Indigenous-led investment entity representing 12 First Nations along the Coastal GasLink (CGL) corridor, including Cheslatta Carrier Nation; Kitselas First Nation; Lheidli T’enneh First Nation; Nadleh Whut’en First Nation, Nee Tahi Buhn Indian Band; Saik’uz First Nation; Skin Tyee Nation; Stellat'en First Nation; Ts’il Kaz Koh First Nation; Wet’suwet’en First Nation; Witset First Nation; and Yekooche First Nation.

Through the agreement, participating Nations have acquired an economic interest in the entity that holds TC Energy’s limited partner interest in CGL. These communities are expected to benefit from long-term predictable financial returns associated with TC Energy’s limited partner interest in CGL.

This transaction marks the second Indigenous investment involving TC Energy's interest in CGL and reflects years of partnership with Indigenous communities along the corridor.

Creating opportunities through partnership

“This transaction demonstrates what is possible when Indigenous communities, industry and governments come together with a shared commitment to creating opportunities that deliver benefits over the long term,” said François Poirier, President and Chief Executive Officer of TC Energy. “It reflects the strength of the relationships developed along the Coastal GasLink corridor over more than a decade of collaboration and our shared belief that major projects should create lasting value for the communities connected to them.”

“This investment represents a historic milestone for our Nations and a new chapter in our relationship with Coastal GasLink,” said Corrina Leween, Director & Executive Committee member, CGL FNLP. “It reflects years of work to advance Indigenous participation in major infrastructure projects and to create a stronger role for our Nations in shaping the economic future of our territories. Through this transaction, our Nations will benefit from a long-term economic interest that provides stable, predictable returns for our communities, helping support future generations and strengthen our collective prosperity. Today’s achievement would not have been possible without the vision and leadership of the late Niilo Edwards, whose commitment to Indigenous economic empowerment helped bring our Nations together around this opportunity.”

Expanding pathways to participation

This transaction was supported by a loan guarantee made available under the Canada Indigenous Loan Guarantee Program, administered by the Canada Indigenous Loan Guarantee Corporation (CILGC).

“We commend TC Energy for working with CGL First Nations Limited Partnership to advance this investment. Partnerships like this can support a more inclusive approach to infrastructure development while strengthening Indigenous economic self-determination and creating opportunities for Nations to share in long-term, project benefits,” said Kristan Straub, President and CEO, Canada Indigenous Loan Guarantee Corporation.

“At a time when Canada must build big things again, in partnership with Indigenous Peoples, projects like Coastal GasLink are helping us strengthen our economic sovereignty, diversify our trade, advance reconciliation and Indigenous prosperity, and secure our place as a global energy superpower. By combining Indigenous economic participation with the investment certainty needed to advance major projects, we are responsibly driving Canada's next generation of growth,” said the Honourable Tim Hodgson, Minister of Energy and Natural Resources.

“Economic reconciliation is about ensuring that Indigenous communities have the opportunity to own, invest in, and benefit from the major projects shaping Canada’s future. This investment will support 12 First Nations in acquiring an interest in, and derive meaningful long-term benefits from, one of Canada’s most important energy infrastructure projects. By helping unlock Indigenous ownership in major projects, we are creating opportunities to build long-term wealth, generate sustainable revenues, and advance economic self-determination for generations to come,” said the Honourable François-Philippe Champagne, Minister of Finance and National Revenue.

Building on more than a decade of partnership

For many participating Nations, this agreement represents the next chapter in a relationship with CGL that spans more than a decade.

The investment opportunity was made available to all 20 Indigenous communities with existing CGL agreements. Participation reflects the independent decisions of each Nation based on its own priorities and objectives.

On Oct. 13, 2026, TC Energy announced its first Indigenous investment agreement related to CGL, involving participating Nations represented through FN CGL Pipeline Limited Partnership. Together, the two agreements build on years of partnership and create additional opportunities for Indigenous communities to benefit from the long-term financial returns associated with TC Energy's limited partner interest in CGL.

A critical pathway for Canadian LNG exportsAs operator and co-owner of CGL, TC Energy safely delivers 2.1 billion cubic feet per day of Canadian natural gas to LNG Canada in Kitimat, B.C., supporting Canadian LNG exports to global markets. With the announcement of CGL Phase 2, system capacity will nearly double, demonstrating the growing global demand for natural gas and long-term value of Canadian LNG exports.

Transaction advisorsRBC Capital Markets acted as financial advisor to TC Energy and Blake, Cassels & Graydon LLP as legal counsel.

For CGL First Nations Limited Partnership, National Bank of Canada Capital Markets acted as business and financial advisors, and Gowling WLG acted as legal counsel.

About TC EnergyWe are a leader in North American energy infrastructure, spanning Canada, the U.S. and Mexico. For over 75 years, we have proudly connected the world to the energy it needs. Every day, we move more than 30 per cent of the natural gas used across the continent and connect LNG exports to global markets—powering communities and industries. Complemented by strategic ownership and low-risk investments in power generation, our infrastructure delivers affordable, reliable and sustainable energy across North America.

We carry forward a legacy of nation building energy infrastructure and strong partnerships. By working with communities, businesses and leaders across our extensive energy network, we create opportunities today and for generations to come.

TC Energy’s common shares trade on the Toronto (TSX) and New York (NYSE) stock exchanges under the symbol TRP. To learn more, visit us at TCEnergy.com.

About Coastal GasLinkCGL is Canada’s first direct pathway to global LNG export markets. It is a 670-kilometre (416-mile) natural gas pipeline that safely delivers 2.1 Bcf/d of natural gas from northeastern British Columbia to the LNG Canada facility in Kitimat, B.C., where it is liquefied for export to global markets. The infrastructure is owned by Coastal GasLink Pipeline Limited Partnership, with TC Energy as the operator.

About CGL First Nations Limited PartnershipCGL First Nations Limited Partnership comprises of 12 First Nations that will collectively hold an economic interest in the entity holding TC Energy’s limited partner interest in the Coastal GasLink project. The partnership was established to pursue collective economic opportunities and advance Indigenous ownership in the Coastal GasLink project, creating long-term benefits for participating Nations and future generations.

data.title: New Zealand consumer confidence hits 10-month high as fuel prices fall
data.description:
New Zealand's consumer confidence rebounded in November to its highest level since January, as shoppers grew more upbeat on the back of falling fuel prices at the pump, ANZ-Roy Morgan data showed on Friday.

The consumer confidence index rose to 100.2 in November, up from 96.2 in October, as two-year inflation expectations eased to their lowest level in nearly two years. A reading above 100 indicates optimism, while a reading below 100 signals pessimism.

"Consumers (are) feeling more chipper about their future prospects than their current circumstances. Still, it was good to see both the current and future conditions indexes rise this month," the survey said.

data.title: Organto Foods Delivers Record Third Quarter 2026 Results
data.description:
Third Quarter Sales +67% Versus PY

Third Consecutive Positive Adjusted EBITDA Quarter

Balance Sheet Remains Strong

VANCOUVER, BC AND BREDA, THE NETHERLANDS / ACCESS Newswire / November 26, 2026 / Organto Foods Inc. ("Organto" or "the Company"), is pleased to announce its financial results for the three and nine-month periods ended September 30, 2026. All amounts are expressed in Canadian dollars and in accordance with International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS), except where specifically noted.

"Q-3 2026 was another record quarter for our Company. Our third quarter sales grew 67% to $25.2 million, the largest third quarter sales in the history of the Company, while gross profit, adjusted gross profit (1) and adjusted EBITDA (1) also reached third quarter records. Equally important, our balance sheet remains strong with $14.5 million of working capital, no long-term debt and net equity of $15.6 million. Following our business repositioning through 2024 and early 2025, our goal was to continue to expand our commercial and operating base, while positioning to achieve positive adjusted EBITDA (1) in 2026. We have realized these objectives and in fact this quarter represents our third consecutive quarter of positive adjusted EBITDA (1) results, demonstrating the strength and adaptability of our scalable, capital-efficient ecosystem. These results reinforce our confidence in the opportunities that lie ahead as we continue to build a world-class organic and fairtrade foods company." commented Steve Bromley, Co-Chair and Chief Executive Officer.

Key Highlights

  • Sales increased 67% to a third quarter record of $25.2 million. Largest third quarter sales in Company's history.
  • Adjusted gross profit (1) when accounting for the impact of currency hedging related to gross profit increased to $2.1 million or 8.2% of sales, an increase of 206% versus the prior year. Largest third quarter gross profit and adjusted gross profit (1) dollars in the Company's history.
  • Cash overhead expenses (1) decreased to 7.8% of sales versus 8.9% in the prior year, demonstrating continued operating leverage.
  • Adjusted EBITDA (1) improved to $0.3 million from a loss of $0.7 million in the prior year. Largest third quarter adjusted EBITDA (1) in the Company's history.
  • Annualized sales run rate (2) continues in excess of $100 million.
  • Working capital increased to $14.5 million.
  • No long-term debt outstanding.
  • Cash balance remained strong at $7.9 million.
  • Equity of $15.6 million, up 78% versus December 31, 2025

Steve Bromley further commented, "We remain focused and committed to building a world-class organic and fairtrade foods company serving growing global healthy and sustainable foods markets, with the goal of creating long-term value for our operating partners, customers, team members and shareholders. We continue to gain momentum in our business and believe our third quarter results reflect another important point in our journey. At the same time, we are working to expand our geographic footprint and product mix with the goal of increasing our market presence and operating margins through increased value-add."

Fiscal 2026 Third Quarter Results Overview

  • Third quarter 2026 sales of $25.2 million versus $15.1 million in the prior year, an increase of approximately 67%. Sales increased as new business was on-boarded and existing customers increased their sales versus the prior year. Sales for the third quarter of 2026 are the largest third quarter sales in the Company's history.
  • Gross profit of $1.5 million or 5.8% of sales, versus $1.2 million or 8.2% of sales in the prior year, an increase of approximately 18% in gross profit dollars. Adjusted gross profit (1) of $2.1 million or 8.2% of sales when accounting for the impact of realized gains on derivatives related to gross profit versus $0.7 million or 4.5% of sales in the prior year, an increase of approximately 206%. Gross profit and adjusted gross profit (1) dollars for the third quarter of 2026 are the largest third quarter gross profit dollars in the history of the Company.
  • Cash overhead expenses (1) of $2.0 million or7.8% of sales versus $1.3 million or 8.9% of sales in the prior year. Cash overhead expenses (1) as a percentage of sales improved versus the prior periods as the business continues to grow and scale and overheads are leveraged on an expanded platform. Costs increased with the addition of administrative and logistics resources required to support significant growth in the business and include $0.2 million related to future oriented corporate development costs.
  • Income from operations (1) excluding stock-based compensation and including realized gains/losses on derivatives related to gross profit of $0.0 million versus a loss of $0.7 million in the prior year.
  • Net interest and accretion costs of $0.1 million versus $0.1 million in the prior year, reflecting lower costs as debt was repaid or restructured in the first half of 2025, resulting in no long-term debt being outstanding as of September 30, 2026.
  • Realized gain of $0.6 million on derivatives versus a loss of $0.6 million in the third quarter of 2025. Unrealized loss on derivative assets of $0.5 million versus an unrealized gain of $1.0 million in the prior year. Derivative assets represent hedges on foreign currencies which are intended to protect the Company's gross profit.
  • Net loss for the third quarter of $1.4 million versus a net loss of $2.0 million in the third quarter of the prior year. Prior year results include a loss on the settlement of debt of $1.7 million and restructuring costs of $0.1 million related to the restructuring of the balance sheet which occurred in 2025.

Fiscal 2026 Nine-Month Results Overview

  • Sales of $78.5 million versus $45.9 million in the prior year, an increase of approximately 71%. Sales increased throughout the first three quarters as new business was on-boarded and existing customers increased their sales versus the prior year.
  • Gross profit of $5.3 million or 6.8% of sales, versus $3.6 million or 7.9% of sales in the prior year, an increase of approximately 48% in gross profit dollars. Adjusted gross profit (1) dollars of $5.9 million or 7.5% of sales when accounting for the impact of realized gains/ losses on derivatives related to gross profit versus $2.5 million or 5.5% of sales in the prior year, an increase of approximately 134%.
  • Cash overhead expenses (1) of $5.3 million or 6.8% of sales versus $3.4 million or 7.4% of sales in the prior year. Cash overhead expenses (1) as a percentage of sales improved versus the prior period as the business continues to grow and scale and overheads are leveraged on an expanded platform. Costs include $0.2 million related to future oriented corporate development expenses.
  • Income from operations (1) excluding stock-based compensation and including realized gains/losses on derivatives related to gross profit of $0.3 million versus a loss of $1.0 million in the prior year.
  • Net interest and accretion costs of $0.2 million versus $0.6 million in the prior year, reflecting lower borrowing costs as debt was repaid or restructured in the first half of 2025, resulting in no long-term debt being outstanding as of September 30, 2026.
  • Realized gain on derivatives of $0.5 million versus a loss of $1.1 million in the prior year. Unrealized gain on derivative assets of $1.0 million versus an unrealized loss of $1.2 million in the prior year. Derivative assets represent hedges on foreign currencies which are intended to protect the Company's gross profit.
  • Net loss of $1.7 million versus a loss of $9.6 million in the prior year. Prior year results include a loss on the settlement of debt of $5.5 million and restructuring costs of $0.8 million, related to the restructuring of the balance sheet which occurred in 2025.

Investor Conference Call

The Company will host a conference call for investors and analysts to discuss its third quarter 2026 financial results on December 1, 2026, at 12:00 pm EST. Organto Food's CEO and Co-Chair, Steve Bromley and President, Darryl Bergman, will provide a corporate update, review the financial results, and discuss the Company's outlook, followed by a Q&A session.

Steve Bromley

(1) The information presented herein refers to the non-IFRS financial measures of adjusted gross profit, cash overhead expenses, income from operations and adjusted EBITDA. (i) Adjusted gross profit - we hedge currencies for certain product categories where either the supply or sales commitments are fixed in foreign currencies. The realized gains and losses from these hedging activities are combined with gross profit to determine adjusted gross profit. (ii) Cash overhead expenses - refers to the combination of selling, general and administration expenses, management fees and labour costs and benefits less non-cash costs included in these expense categories. (iii) Income from operations - refers to the net result of the net loss for the period excluding non-cash stock-based compensation, interest expense and accretion, other income, unrealized gains/losses on derivative assets and liabilities, restructuring costs, gain (loss) on the settlement of debt and foreign exchange gains (losses). data.title: Final New Zealand election vote count to confirm parliament make up
data.description:
Final government election results are due to be released in New Zealand later on Friday, with the official count expected to confirm whether the incumbent centre-right government can hold on to its razor-slim majority.

Preliminary results released by New Zealand’s Electoral Commission after the November 7 election showed the incumbent three-party ruling coalition led by National had a majority of two seats, after an election dominated by a struggling economy and voter ​disillusionment with the two biggest contenders.

The final results released on Friday will include around 400,000 special votes, which include ballots cast overseas and those requiring additional checks. Those votes have typically favoured the left, with parties on the right losing support following the count. This could also ​be key in seats where races remain tight between Labour and National candidates.

Party leaders are expected to respond after the results are published, as negotiations over a possible governing arrangement gather pace.

Under New Zealand's proportional representation system, parties frequently need support agreements with smaller partners to form an administration.

There are 71 constituency seats and at least 49 party seats, and a party or coalition needs a majority to form a government.

The final tally will also settle the number of electorate and list seats won by each party, providing a clearer picture of the balance of power for the next parliamentary term.

data.title: Targinta secures patents in Europe, China and the USA for integrin α10 antibodies in aggressive cancers
data.description:
Targinta (subsidiary of Xintela) announces that the company has been granted new patents in three major markets for its integrin α10 antibody technology: a European patent for triple-negative breast cancer, a Chinese patent that also covers other aggressive cancers, and a second US patent for the diagnosis of brain tumours.

The European Patent Office has granted EP 3 956 360, which covers antibodies that bind integrin α10 and inhibit the growth of cancer cells, for the treatment of triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), as well as methods for diagnosis and prognosis. The patent has unitary effect in 18 EU member states, is also in force in the United Kingdom and Switzerland, and can be maintained until April 2040.

The China National Intellectual Property Administration has granted patent ZL 202080043354.8, covering defined integrin α10 antibodies for the treatment and diagnosis of TNBC and other aggressive cancers, including lung and pancreatic cancer. This patent is also in force until April 2040.

The US Patent and Trademark Office has issued US 12,806,280, Targinta's second US patent in the patent family for tumours of the central nervous system. The patent covers methods for detecting integrin α10 in samples from the central nervous system in order to identify tumours. Covered tumour types include glioma and glioblastoma, and the patent is in force until September 2037. The patent family is also granted in Europe, Japan and several other countries.

“These patents provide our integrin α10 antibodies broader protection and strengthen our patent position in several major markets. Together with our product patent applications for TARG9 and TARG10, this gives Targinta and future partners a strong foundation for exclusivity in some of the most aggressive and difficult-to-treat cancers”, says Evy Lundgren-Åkerlund, CEO of Targinta.

About Xintela och Targinta

Xintela (XINT) is a publicly-traded clinical-stage biopharma company developing cutting edge medical products in stem cell therapy and targeted cancer therapy. Xintela’s proprietary technology uses the stem cell marker integrin α10β1 to select and quality-assure stem cells in the product XSTEM®, which has shown safety and positive efficacy in a clinical study on knee osteoarthritis and has completed a clinical study on difficult-to-heal leg ulcers. Xintela’s in-house GMP-facility manufactures XSTEM and provides process development and manufacturing of other cell therapies. Xintela’s wholly owned subsidiary Targinta AB develops First-in-Class therapeutic antibodies targeting integrin α10β1. TARG9, an Antibody-Drug Conjugate (ADC), and TARG10, a function blocking antibody, are in preclinical development for the treatment of aggressive, difficult-to-treat cancers including glioblastoma, triple-negative breast cancer and sarcoma. Xintela conducts its business at Medicon Village in Lund, Sweden, and is listed on Nasdaq First North Growth Market Stockholm. Xintela's Certified Adviser is Västra Hamnen Corporate Finance AB..

data.title: Brazil leads LatAm assets higher after cooler-than-expected inflation data
data.description:
Key points:
  • MSCI LatAm stock index rises 3%, FX up 1.3%
  • Argentina's Senate to weigh crucial bill
  • Mexico central bank lifts 2026 growth forecast after stronger third quarter
  • US, Qatar to help Venezuela clear regional development bank arrears, sources say

By Niket Nishant and Johann M Cherian

Brazilian stocks surged on Thursday and were on track for their strongest day in over seven weeks after data showed inflation eased in mid-November, helping investors shrug off the latest tariff threats from Washington.

The Bovespa index was last up 4.4%, the biggest gainer in Latin America, while the real strengthened 1.4% versus the US dollar and 2.1% versus the Mexican peso .

The IPCA-15 consumer price index rose less than expected in the month through mid-November, data showed, raising investor expectations the local central bank could start considering lowering interest rates if the trend continues.

The gains could help investors look past the fresh tariff threat from the US. Washington proposed adding new tariffs on goods from Brazil on Wednesday, ​including a 10% duty on finished aircraft, arguing Brasilia had failed to rectify what it calls "unreasonable" trade practices.

Separately, Brazil's finance minister Dario Durigan said he will hold a follow-up meeting with President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva later on Thursday to discuss additional fiscal measures aimed at curbing spending.

MSCI's index of regional equities (.MILA00000PUS) gained 2.9%, while the corresponding currency gauge (.MILA00000CUS) rose 1.3%.

"EM equities look positioned for robust performance in 2027, supported by double-digit earnings growth, inexpensive valuations, an oversold starting point, and structural AI capex tailwinds," JPMorgan analysts wrote in a note.

The brokerage has an "overweight" rating on regional sovereign bonds, but is underweight currencies as it expects the US Federal Reserve to raise rates.

Higher rates in the US typically boost the dollar, thereby weakening emerging market currencies.

ARGENTINA'S SENATE POISED TO SUSPEND PRIMARIES

Argentine stocks (.MMXMRVLGA) shot up 3.2% and the peso gained 0.2% as the country's Senate weighed a bill that would suspend primary elections.

If suspended it would be a potential win for President Javier Milei ahead of next year's presidential race as the country teeters on the brink of a recession.

Mexican stocks shed 1.6% after logging the strongest daily jump since June in the previous session, while the peso slipped 0.6%.

The country's central bank raised its 2026 economic growth forecast to 1.9% after stronger-than-expected activity in the third quarter, even as it warned investment is likely to remain subdued because of uncertainty over trade ties with the United States.

Separately, the country sought a meeting with US aviation authorities to discuss permits for SpaceX to use Mexican airspace and potentially relocate its launch activities, following tensions between Mexico City and Elon Musk's trillion-dollar company.

Peru's sol and stocks (.MXNUAMPESCPGPE) were steady after President Keiko Fujimori said the country will receive a $10 billion loan from the Inter-American Development Bank over four years.

Venezuelan bonds were also steady, following a two-day rally on debt restructuring hopes.

The country is also working on separate bridge loans with the US Treasury and Qatar to clear arrears owed to two regional development banks, a move that could unlock fresh multilateral financing for the cash-strapped country, sources told Reuters.

Elsewhere, Turkey's Finance Minister Mehmet Simsek said the country expects to complete work to meet MSCI's requirements by the end of December, ahead of the index provider's June 2027 deadline, as Ankara seeks to bring its capital markets in line with international standards after an investment funds crisis.

The country's equities index closed up 0.8% earlier in the day.

Trading was relatively subdued because of the US Thanksgiving holiday.

data.title: Bitcoin Miners Go 98 Minutes Without Finding a Single Block
data.description:
Bitcoin miners experienced their longest dry spell since July on Nov. 26. According to Galaxy's Alex Thorn, it took Bitcoin miners 98 minutes and 19 seconds to find the next block.

That's the third time in 2026 that miners have gone this long without finding a block. The wait ended at 18:28 UTC on Thursday.

For anyone trying to get Bitcoin transactions confirmed shortly after the previous block, the gap meant waiting more than an hour and a half.

Even if you paid a very high transaction fee, you would still have to wait until a miner found the next block before your transaction could receive its first confirmation.

Thursday's gap was the 69th longest since 2011, according to Galaxy Research. It was just three minutes shy of the threshold for the top 50.

And this year's other long gap lasted nearly two hours. On July 6, miners took 112 minutes and 26 seconds to find the next block (number 956,953). That was the 19th longest gap on record, according to Galaxy.

How can a 10-minute interval result in a 98-minute wait?

Bitcoin automatically adjusts mining difficulty every 2,016 blocks to keep the average block interval at around 10 minutes.

However, blocks sometimes are found seconds apart. Other times, it takes well over an hour for the next block to be found.

At any given mining difficulty, the chance that a single attempt to find a block will succeed is incredibly small.

If miners have spent 90 minutes trying to find the next block, the chance of succeeding on the next attempt is the same as it was on the first attempt.

So the expected time until the next block is found is still 10 minutes, even if it's already been 90 minutes since the last block was found. That's assuming the network's total computing power and mining difficulty remain unchanged.

Assuming an average block interval of 10 minutes, Thorn said you could expect a gap of at least 98 minutes and 19 seconds about once every 18,600 block intervals.

That means such a gap should occur roughly once every four months, based on an average of about 144 blocks per day.

How the historical rankings can change

Galaxy examined 877,290 block intervals going back to Jan. 1, 2011.

Researchers identified 1,948 intervals where at least an hour had passed between the timestamps of successive blocks.

However, Galaxy flagged 97 of those intervals because an adjacent block had a timestamp that was off by at least 10 minutes. This raised questions about the actual length of those gaps.

The longest recorded interval is particularly interesting.

On Nov. 30, 2011, block 155,290 seemingly marked the end of a 144-minute-and-50-second gap.

However, the miner who found the next block had set its timestamp back by 65 minutes.

After excluding apparent timestamp errors, the longest gap was 141 minutes and one second, recorded on Oct. 13, 2011.
